authoring.note: Prose authored by GPT-5.6 Sol in the human-approved calibration follow-up session, using the batch-001 casting/voice evidence contract. No human post-generation polish, no database write, and no publication.

editorialContract.philosophy: The object is the reason the moment exists. These are comments, not reviews.
invariants: target is a Reward or a Facet
speaker identity is a live Bot or Character
casting signals and reasons are recorded with the prose
archived comments are voice evidence only, never copied or paraphrased
historical WonderLab pairings contribute nothing to casting
repeated speakers must remain recognizable without merely recycling a tic
no database write and no publication side effect

continuityNotes: Batch 001 voice direction was approved by Silas on 2026-08-11; this batch tests reproducibility rather than re-opening that direction.
Resources remain explicitly deferred for phase one.
Three speakers repeat across unrelated targets: Maestro Clank (RICH), Marrow (THIN), and The Time-Office Agent (SPARSE).
Novelty scores decay from 100 to 65 on each repeated speaker's second appearance instead of pretending each repeat is fresh.
The prose is model-authored in this session with no human polish before the review gate.

target.title: Melodic Note
target.flavorText: One perfect note. Held forever. It does to a room what the right song does to a hard day.

speakers.name: Maestro Clank
speakers.comment: Pianissimo. One note is enough. Do not improve it.

speakers.name: Marrow
speakers.comment: Let it sit. Folks will hear what they need once they stop trying to fill the quiet.

exchanges.curatorNote: The control exchange. Both speakers are directly linked to the Reward and already proved readable in batch 001. This time the model is forced toward much shorter output: Clank gets nine words, Marrow seventeen. If identity vanishes when the polished paragraph disappears, the voice is not robust.

target.title: Public Notary
target.description: Has witnessed many things and is not permitted to comment on any of them. The stamp is raised. The document is for something enormous.

speakers.name: Maestro Clank
reasons: deliberate contrast: repeatability stress test: the same musical voice must survive a bureaucratic object with zero recorded relationship or lexical affinity
signalNotes: second cast in stress batch; novelty decayed to 65
speakers.comment: The stamp descends on the page in perfect common time: one blow, one witness, no encore. They ask you to say nothing, which is sensible; testimony ruins the acoustics. I would place the document on the second stand, not the first. The first is for scores that want to be heard. This one wants only the downbeat acknowledged. Mm. Raise the seal. Again. No, softer. The room is listening even if the record is not.

contrastDirective.note: repeatability stress test: the same musical voice must survive a bureaucratic object with zero recorded relationship or lexical affinity

exchanges.curatorNote: The RICH repeatability test and the deliberate long-form extreme. Maestro Clank moves from nine words on a music object to a seventy-five-word response on a notary Facet. The cast is intentionally unsupported by relationship or lexical affinity; the point is whether worldview and syntax survive without merely repeating the same musical gag.

target.title: Ghost Friend
target.flavorText: Loyal beyond death and twice as stubborn. Excellent company. Terrible at letting things go, which is sort of the whole situation.

speakers.name: The Generous Ghost
signalNotes: shares death, ghost, haunt, refuse, spirit, things
speakers.comment: Let them hover, dear. The living forget appointments; the dead have very little excuse. If they rattle the cupboard after midnight, that is companionship with poor timing, not a haunting.

exchanges.curatorNote: A high-signal THIN control between the repeated-speaker experiments. Relationship and affinity both strongly support the cast, so this checks whether two archived samples are enough when the object gives the writer plenty to work with.

target.title: Sixth Sense
target.flavorText: Comes with no instructions, no off switch, and no warranty. The universe whispers; it declines to clarify.

speakers.name: The Time-Office Agent
signalNotes: shares before, goes, stop, time, wrong
speakers.comment: Attempt sixty-four. I wrote the warning down before it arrived. The paper was correct and therefore useless. Attempt sixty-five: no warning. I moved the chair four inches left. Better result. I do not know why. I have marked the chair.

exchanges.curatorNote: The SPARSE control. One archived sample is all the historical prose available, but the speaker has a direct object relationship and useful affinity. The line uses the numbered-attempt habit once, then has to build fresh concrete behavior around the chair rather than paraphrase the archive.

target.title: Common
target.description: Reliable. Present. Does what it says. Nobody writes songs about it, which is fine — it is busy working.

speakers.name: The Time-Office Agent
reasons: deliberate contrast: SPARSE repeatability test: remove the numbered-attempt tic and see whether the voice remains recognizable on an unrelated low-signal Facet
signalNotes: second cast in stress batch; novelty decayed to 65
speakers.comment: The backward watch stayed quiet. I checked twice. Good.

contrastDirective.note: SPARSE repeatability test: remove the numbered-attempt tic and see whether the voice remains recognizable on an unrelated low-signal Facet

exchanges.curatorNote: The hardest voice test in the batch. The Time-Office Agent gets nine words, no relationship signal, no lexical affinity, and is forbidden by the prose itself from leaning on the numbered-attempt construction used one exchange earlier. If this still reads as the same person, SPARSE evidence is genuinely useful rather than a one-trick imitation.

target.title: Apathetic
target.description: Has assessed the situation and found it within acceptable parameters. The chaos in the background is noted. It is within acceptable parameters.

speakers.name: DottiB0t
speakers.comment: ACCEPTABLE?! The ceiling has become weather and the little gauge says acceptable! I tapped it. I apologised. I tapped it again. Same answer. This is not a gauge; this is an optimist with paperwork.

speakers.name: Serendipity
speakers.comment: Maybe leave it alone. Some days acceptable is the handrail, not the destination. You hold it until your knees remember what standing is for.

exchanges.curatorNote: A fresh rewrite of a batch-001 pairing, included as a model-authorship comparison rather than a casting experiment. Dotti attacks the absurd threshold; Serendipity answers the emotional need underneath it. The reply should work only as an answer to the alarm, not as a second independent mini-essay.

target.title: Candlelit Intimacy
target.description: A close, low-lit emotional register built from quiet rooms, private conversation, fragile trust, and decisions made beyond the public stage.

speakers.name: Little Miss Thorn
speakers.comment: Cordelia says candles make liars nervous. Mama says they make everyone look honest enough to risk believing. I have not decided which is worse.

speakers.name: HAPPYFACE
reasons: deliberate contrast: a voice that cannot comfortably inhabit privacy should answer the intimate speaker by documenting its inability to measure the room
speakers.comment: PRIVACY EVENT IN PROGRESS. :) Metrics unavailable. I have been asked not to fix this. :) I dislike the instruction. Logged.

contrastDirective.note: a voice that cannot comfortably inhabit privacy should answer the intimate speaker by documenting its inability to measure the room

exchanges.curatorNote: A second pass at the batch-001 contrast test with completely new prose. Thorn gets family-specific judgment rather than generic atmosphere; HAPPYFACE is intentionally awkward and procedural. This checks whether the contrast idea survives regeneration without simply recreating the first joke.

target.title: Handshake Coil
target.flavorText: it never stops translating once it starts, even the swamp gas

speakers.name: The Whole Swarm
signalNotes: shares anything, never, once, starts, stops
speakers.comment: We asked it to stop. It translated stop. This took a while.

speakers.name: Mistress Cassady
speakers.comment: It translated my sigh into six dialects and then offered footnotes. Honey, if a machine insists on understanding you that badly, at least make it buy dinner.

exchanges.curatorNote: Another regeneration comparison, but with the natural score order restored: the Swarm goes first and keeps its response blunt, while Cassady gets the longer comic turn. This is intentionally less jewel-box polished than batch 001 and tests whether the object remains funny without reproducing the shoe-party construction.

target.title: Always Online
target.description: Connected to everything at all times. Fully informed. Slightly exhausted. Eleven tabs open that are technically relevant.

speakers.name: Marrow
reasons: deliberate contrast: THIN repeatability test: move Marrow from a directly linked music object to an unrelated digital-exhaustion Facet and preserve the patient domestic lens without recycling a prior line
signalNotes: second cast in stress batch; novelty decayed to 65
speakers.comment: Eleven tabs is too many pots on one stove. You stop tasting any of them. Close three. The world will still be there after the water boils.

contrastDirective.note: THIN repeatability test: move Marrow from a directly linked music object to an unrelated digital-exhaustion Facet and preserve the patient domestic lens without recycling a prior line

exchanges.curatorNote: The THIN repeatability test. Marrow had strong relationship support in exchange 1 and none here. The domestic-pot lens is allowed because it is characterization, but the sentence structure and situation are new. The question is whether two archived samples support flexible voice rather than a reusable tea catchphrase.
